name: beacon_score
description: Measure how tightly a series of event times clusters around its median interval: the median interval, the median absolute deviation and mad_over_median, a descriptive shape (tight_cluster, clustered, loose_cluster, dispersed; the cut-offs are conventions of this tool, not properties of any implant), event_density_ratio (distinct events over the count a constant schedule at the median would give; below 1 is not evidence that events are missing), duplicate times counted apart from distinct events, and every interval kept (a bounded page inline, the whole list in a file the answer names, each interval with the positions in the supplied series of the two events it joins). A regular series is not malicious (update checks, telemetry, NTP and monitoring are more regular than most malware) and an irregular one says nothing about a destination: a score is a measurement, not a verdict. long_final_gap reports a last interval over four times the median that ended in an observed event; it is not a cessation. A statement about silence after the last event is made only when window_end and sensor_coverage_confirmed are both given, and is a bounded negative about this series. A time with no zone is refused unless assume_utc is true (and each such value is counted); NaN, infinite or non-epoch-second values are counted and named, never scored, and any such value makes the answer partial (all_values_scored false, the counts in status_basis): the measurements cover the values that were scored. The series is what the caller supplied: this tool does not read captures or logs. The series is packed as it is read (about 110 bytes resident per event: 336 MB measured at the 3,000,000-event cap of a timestamps_file, which the tool refuses to go past; a series passed inline is held as parsed JSON as well, so it is capped at 500,000 events and 32 MiB of arguments), and the tool keeps its own clock (max_seconds, default 40, at most 45; the manifest's limit is 60) for reading and measuring together: reading stops at two fifths of it, because the ordering and the measurement after the last value cannot be interrupted and take 0.6 to 0.9 times as long as the reading did (1.4 times with a tenth of a CPU; 3,000,000 events), so a slow CPU still ends with a partial answer inside the limit; if it runs out while reading, the answer measures the values read, says so (status partial, stopped_reading_at_input_index) and exits 0. Every answer carries status (complete, partial or failed) and status_basis. A rejected value is never printed back: first_rejected names its position, the reason and its length only, and a label must be a few plain words. ISO 8601 times are read by the tool's own parser, the same on every Python: YYYY-MM-DD, then T or one space, HH:MM[:SS[.fraction up to 9 digits]], then Z, +hh, +hh:mm or +hhmm; hour 24, second 60 and a bare fraction point are refused. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with partial JSON on stdout and exit 128 plus the signal.

timestamps.description: Event times: epoch seconds, or ISO 8601 strings that carry a zone. Give this or timestamps_file. At most 500,000 events inline (the arguments are parsed whole, and the clock covers reading them); a longer series, up to 3,000,000, goes in timestamps_file

timestamps_file.description: A file with one time per line (for a series too long to pass inline); the same value rules apply. At most 3,000,000 events. A line over 4,096 characters is counted as unreadable and not held

label.description: What this series is, carried into the result: a few plain words (up to 80 printable ASCII characters, with no run of more than 15 letters, digits or _ + / = - without a break); anything else is refused without being echoed

min_events.description: Refuse to score fewer than this many distinct events (default 6, at least 3)

assume_utc.description: Read a time with no zone as UTC (default false: such a time is refused). Every time read this way is counted in naive_timestamps_assumed_utc

window_end.description: When the sensor's coverage of this series ends (epoch seconds or ISO 8601 with a zone). Needed, with sensor_coverage_confirmed, before anything is said about silence after the last event

sensor_coverage_confirmed.description: True only when you know the sensor kept recording over the whole window up to window_end

limit.description: Intervals shown inline (default 40); the whole list is written under $OUT/tool-output (work/<agent>/tool-output outside a job) and named in intervals_page

out_dir.description: Optional empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT; work/<your agent id>/name is mapped to $OUT/name) for intervals.tsv, every interval with its two times and their input positions

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock for reading and measuring the series, from 1 to 45 seconds (default 40); reading stops at two fifths of it. When it runs out the answer measures the values read and says so (status partial)
